twrite.en: Because light needs time to cross the enormous gaps between stars, what we see in the night sky is a picture of the past, not the present.
twrite.theme: 충분히 멀리 있으면 이미 꺼진 태양도 계속 빛나 보인다 — 빛은 빠르지만 무한히 빠르지는 않다

twrite.en: The belief that the economy stands at the center of the world is giving way to the view that it is one part of the web of life, and we must hurry that change along.

twrite.ko: 기술이 불평등을 부추기고 일자리를 없애면서, 시장은 점점 더 많은 사람에게 사회의 부를 나눠 주는 일을 멈출지도 모른다.
twrite.en: As technology drives inequality and destroys jobs, the market may stop delivering a share of society's wealth to a growing number of people.

para.en: ❶ In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States. ❷ In the study, they found that individuals who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of assistance because of other-focused motives were almost four times more likely to still be giving support one year later than those whose original motivation was to reduce personal distress. ❸ This effect likely stems from differences in emotional arousal. ❹ The events of September 11th emotionally affected people throughout the United States. ❺ Those who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress. ❻ However, those who gave to reduce others’ distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks.

❶ As always happens with natural selection, bats and their prey have been engaged in a life-or-death sensory arms race for millions of years. ❷ It’s believed that hearing in moths arose specifically in response to the threat of being eaten by bats. ❸ Over millions of years, moths have evolved the ability to detect sounds at ever higher frequencies, and, as they have, the frequencies of bats’ vocalizations have risen, too. ❹ Some moth species have also evolved scales on their wings and a fur-like coat on their bodies; both act as “acoustic camouflage,” by absorbing sound waves in the frequencies emitted by bats, thereby preventing those sound waves from bouncing back. ❺ The B-2 bomber and other “stealth” aircraft have fuselages made of materials that do something similar with radar beams.

❶ Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. ❷ These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. ❸ For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. ❹ A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. ❺ Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? ❻ Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they’re in better condition when resold? ❼ Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses, and our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. ❽ Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can’t easily do the same for causal links. ❾ So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.

❶ Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. ❷ Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. ❸ Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. ❹ When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. ❺ In other words, an “empathic” company understands the needs and wants of its customers, and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. ❻ When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations — the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on — when designing products.

❶ On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. ❷ If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it’s physically where we see it, shining away. ❸ We reach out our hand and touch it: It’s there all right, and unpleasantly hot. ❹ If the filament fails, then the light goes out; we don’t see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it’s removed from its socket. ❺ The very notion seems nonsensical. ❻ But if we’re far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we’ll continue to see it shining brightly; we won’t learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come — in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. ❼ The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.

❶ One well-known shift took place when the accepted view — that the Earth was the center of the universe — changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. ❷ With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. ❸ So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. ❹ This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. ❺ When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. ❻ Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. ❼ By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.

❶ Over the last few centuries, humanity’s collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. ❷ To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. ❸ But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. ❹ Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. ❺ And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. ❻ As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society’s prosperity at all.
